solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird to move over river descending on one fish

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
the Roman numeral I stands for one
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A bird is told to shift across a river and swoop down on a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' and 'descending on' are placement words: the first piece sits above the river letter, and both drop onto the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgerigar is a small Australian parrot, a familiar cage bird.

clue.text: Notice the female and male finally forming bond

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
her is the female pronoun

indicators.note: finally signals taking just the last letter of the word male

explanation.surface: A notice describes a woman and a man ending up forming a bond.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast, so bond as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: One now down having been up successfully?

definitions.text: One now down having been up successfully?

parts.words: One now down having been up successfully?
parts.note: at British universities a student is 'up' while in residence and goes 'down' on leaving; someone who left after completing a degree successfully

explanation.surface: Someone who climbed well is now down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' and 'down' suggest climbing or mood, but at Oxford and Cambridge you go up to university and come down when you leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who completed a degree has left university with success, the cryptic picture.

clue.text: Look — Queen going out and greeting Commonwealth PM!

indicators.note: going out tells us the Queen's letters leave the word for a look

parts.note: a gander is a look, as in 'take a gander'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: An exclamation as the Queen leaves and greets a Commonwealth prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ER from GANDER leaves GAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Indira Gandhi was prime minister of India, a Commonwealth country.

clue.text: Serious fault-finding

definitions.meaning: a ... condition is grave or dangerous

explanation.definitionFit: Critical means both grave in state and inclined to criticise others.

clue.text: Girl keeps going, wasting little time

indicators.note: wasting suggests losing something, here the time abbreviation dropped

parts.note: something that lasts keeps going
T is a short form of time

explanation.surface: A girl carries on, though she squanders the little time she has.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a mainly Scottish and northern word for a girl.

clue.text: Opinion-influencer to crumble?

definitions.meaning: someone who moulds opinion shapes it
to rot away slowly into dust or decay

explanation.definitionFit: One who moulds is literally a shaper; as a verb the word means to decay gradually.

clue.text: A van that has novel elements?

definitions.text: A van that has novel elements?

parts.words: A van that has novel elements?
parts.note: novel suggests new ideas, but here it means fiction: a vehicle carrying books for lending

explanation.surface: A vehicle with innovative features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new', but it means novels, the books lent from a travelling van.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling van stocked with books for loan is the vehicle described.

clue.text: A spender finally ends in debt

indicators.note: finally signals only the final letter of spender is used

parts.note: the rears of things are their back ends

explanation.surface: A big spender eventually finds himself owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends in' reads as a single phrase but 'ends' gives REARS and 'in' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are overdue sums still owed, a form of debt.

clue.text: What's accepted, in short, by various punters

definitions.text: What's accepted, in short, by various punters

parts.words: What's accepted, in short, by various punters
parts.note: betting odds shortened to SP that many gamblers take when a race begins

explanation.surface: Something many gamblers agree to, abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' points to the betting abbreviation SP, the odds on offer when a horse race starts.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, bettors who take no fixed odds are paid at the odds prevailing at the off.

clue.text: Conceited and obstinate, wanting new leader

indicators.note: wanting new leader says the first letter of the word for obstinate is swapped for another

parts.note: pigheaded means stubborn and obstinate

explanation.surface: Someone vain and stubborn needs replacing as chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter B is not clued; the change from P to B is what the solver must find from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Big-headed means having an inflated opinion of oneself, as conceited does.

clue.text: Operatic character appearing in panto — scary!

indicators.note: appearing in signals letters found within the following words

explanation.surface: A villainous opera role turns up in a frightening pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Floria Tosca is the heroine of Puccini's opera.

clue.text: Great river in time getting to lake

indicators.note: getting to places the lake letter up against the rest, which follows it

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: in places the river letter inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A great river eventually reaches a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and great are synonyms for big in size.

clue.text: After a drink seek battle

indicators.note: After places the word for seek after the first pieces

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink
to court is to seek, as in courting favour

explanation.surface: Having had a drink, someone goes looking for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 battle in which Henry V defeated the French.

clue.text: See where exhibitor may hide additional goods

definitions.meaning: to see is to grasp or comprehend

definitions.text: where exhibitor may hide additional goods
definitions.meaning: spare stock at a trade fair is kept beneath the display stand

explanation.definitionFit: To see in the sense of 'I see' means to comprehend; the second reading splits the word into under and stand.

clue.text: Messenger, Eastern person who's left something

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or emissary

explanation.surface: An envoy from the East who has left something behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but the person here is one to whom something has been left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a beneficiary who receives a bequest under a will.

clue.text: Trivial lapse almost going on to romantic affair

indicators.note: almost signals the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a slip or mistake
a fling is a brief romantic affair

explanation.surface: A minor slip almost turns into an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifling means of little importance, a synonym of trivial.

clue.text: Sultan having healthy food at home

parts.note: a salad is a healthy dish
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A ruler eating healthily at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century sultan of Egypt and Syria who fought the Crusaders.

clue.text: Officials set out areas for voters

indicators.note: out signals the letters of set are rearranged

parts.note: wards are electoral districts

explanation.surface: Officials organise voting districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' looks like one verb, but 'set' is the fodder and 'out' the anagram signal, giving STE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are officials who manage events such as race meetings.

clue.text: Drug — horse is given it before lunchtime?

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the lunchtime hour

parts.note: a barb is a Barbary horse
one o'clock is a traditional lunchtime

explanation.surface: A horse is dosed with something before lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbitone is a barbiturate sedative drug.

clue.text: Cricketer's leg

parts.note: not a limb: in cricket the leg is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.walkthrough: Leg looks like a body part, but in cricket the leg side is a half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the leg side and the on side are the same half of the field.

clue.text: Expose disreputable person at end of street

indicators.note: at end of places the person after the street abbreviation

parts.note: a rip is a dissolute rake or scoundrel

explanation.surface: Unmask a scoundrel at the end of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to lay bare, which is what exposing does.

clue.text: A lot of sand has upset Arab endlessly

indicators.note: upset signals the letters of has are jumbled
endlessly drops the last letter of the word Arab

explanation.surface: An Arab is said to be annoyed in a vast desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert, an enormous expanse of sand.

clue.text: A knight set to become a messenger

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A knight prepares to carry a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel derives from the Greek for messenger, a divine envoy.

clue.text: Idol keeps a hound

indicators.note: keeps signals one piece is held inside another

parts.note: an idol is a god worshipped

explanation.surface: A god owns a hunting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to goad or harass them persistently.

clue.text: Food eight spat out

indicators.note: spat out suggests letters thrown around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spits out eight mouthfuls of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a type of pasta, an everyday food.

clue.text: Wanted time, study having got put back

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: put back signals the word for study is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Someone longed for time to study but was set back.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearned means longed for, a synonym of wanted.

clue.text: Disorder could make you enraged

indicators.note: could make you hints the letters can be reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: Disorder could make you furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or disarray.
